question: Why is vincristine sulfate short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 2 stock lines across 2 hospitals, 1 presentation, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 1 plant links on 1 labels; 1 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.purpose: Read FDA's current shortage list and its history for this drug.
steps.finding: Not on FDA's current shortage list.

steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

explanation.headline: Vincristine sulfate is not on FDA's shortage list as of 2026-10-21; supply traces to a registered plant with a VAI inspection in 2022 and a prior OAI in 2014

sentences.text: FDA's drug shortage list does not include vincristine sulfate as of 2026-10-21.
The product label for NDC 61703030925 identifies Hospira Australia Pty Ltd (FEI 3001174929) as the registered manufacturing plant.
FDA inspected that plant on 2022-09-02 and classified the inspection VAI.
An earlier inspection ending 2014-03-04 was classified OAI and a Warning Letter was issued on 2014-09-26.
Corvale East holds 64 vials of the 1 mg/mL, 2 mL presentation at 3.1 vials per day, providing 20.4 days on hand.
Corvale General holds 67 vials at 2.9 vials per day, providing 23.3 days on hand.
Check current allocation status with the supplier and monitor FDA communications for any future shortage posting.

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.
